audit_findings.title: The no-perimeter ruling conflicts with major late-2025 transactions
audit_findings.mechanism: The mixed-perimeter 2025 owner-earnings anchor feeds every forecast year and terminal value, while the latest bridge reflects the post-transaction balance sheet.
audit_findings.evidence: On August 29, 2025, MPLX completed the acquisition of 100 percent of the outstanding membership interests of Northwind Delaware Holdings LLC (“Northwind Midstream”) for $ 2.4 billion in cash (the “Northwind Midstream Acquisition”).
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: 2025 includes only four months of Northwind, six months of consolidated BANGL, nearly eleven months of Rockies, and partial acquisition-financing interest, yet perimeter is null. The net owner-earnings effect is not established, but it could materially raise or lower all scenario values because the $4,541.3 million anchor drives the entire DCF.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-transaction owner earnings with full-year Northwind and BANGL, no Rockies contribution, full-year acquisition interest, and no transaction gains or costs; then rerun all scenarios and populate the perimeter field.

audit_findings.title: The $5.149 billion stake bridge may double count equity-method businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $5,149 million of bridge value, or $5.07 per unit; actual overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings or distributions may enter owner earnings while the same investees' $5.149 billion carrying value is added separately through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had $4.8 billion of equity method investments recorded on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filed equity-method investment balance exactly matches stakes_net, but the supplied record does not trace whether the associated income and distributions were removed from the $4,541.3 million owner-earnings anchor. Double counting is therefore an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated full $5.149 billion error. The maximum bridge exposure equals 7.4% of the $69.986 billion base equity value and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each investee's equity income, cash distributions, basis amortization, and maintenance capital through owner earnings. Either remove all investee economics from the numerator before retaining the stake bridge or remove the corresponding stake value and rerun.

audit_findings.title: BANGL earnout is an omitted claim ahead of common units
audit_findings.mechanism: The latest fair-value contingent-consideration liability should reduce the equity bridge unless its expected settlement is already deducted from projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The earnout payment will continue to be remeasured at fair value each quarter with changes in fair value recognized in earnings until either the EBITDA targets are met or the earnout period ends, with the total payout capped at $ 275 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated: the June 2026 filing reports a $235 million liability while the bridge contains no contingent consideration. A full deduction is only 0.34% of the $69.986 billion base equity value and reduces base value from $68.96 to about $68.73 per unit, leaving the $9.86 base-value premium to the $59.105 market price and the no-purchase result versus the $48.27 buy-below level intact. It would, however, reverse the very narrow bear-case comparison to market.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the latest $235 million liability from the bridge and recompute scenario values and the buy-below price; confirm projected owner earnings contain no separate earnout settlement charge.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded joint-venture support obligations are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $187 million maximum potential undiscounted exposure, or $0.18 per unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Triggered guarantee payments would reduce cash attributable to common units or the realizable value of the separately added equity-method stakes.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our maximum potential undiscounted payments under the Contingent Equity Contribution Agreement were approximately $ 78 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $78 million Dakota Access and $109 million WPC exposures are filed maximum contingent amounts, but no triggering payment is established. Dakota Access received a May 2026 Record of Decision supporting continued operation, while future litigation remains possible. These are forward-looking contingent claims totaling 3.6% of stakes_net and 0.27% of base equity value, rather than present valuation errors.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Dakota Access litigation and WPC construction performance; obtain investee valuations showing whether the guarantees are probability-weighted, and rerun the bridge if a payment becomes probable or the stake values do not incorporate the exposures.

audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings have a known NCI basis inconsistency
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent attribution of consolidated depreciation, capital spending, and minority-owned cash flows can distort the historical owner-earnings series and the evidence supporting scenario growth.
audit_findings.evidence: For non-wholly-owned consolidated subsidiaries, the interests owned by third parties have been recorded as Noncontrolling interests on the accompanying Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis inconsistency in 2016, 2017, and 2019 is a demonstrated historical calculation error, but the supplied record gives no attributable amounts. The $4,541.3 million valuation anchor is the latest actual year rather than the historical trend, and the latest-year NCI test reportedly passes. The direct anchor is therefore unaffected, but corrected history could strengthen or weaken the rationale for 3% base and 5% bull growth; materiality cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Restate 2016, 2017, and 2019 using only depreciation, capital spending, earnings, and other adjustments attributable to MPLX, then reassess the growth evidence and rerun scenarios only if the supported growth cases change.

audit_findings.title: The terminal value assumes continued partnership-level tax treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed potential federal rate is 21% plus state and local taxes
audit_findings.mechanism: Loss of partnership treatment would introduce recurring entity-level taxes into owner earnings, reducing forecast cash flows and the terminal value, which supplies 47.7% to 50.9% of scenario operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: If we were treated as a corporation for federal income tax purposes, we would pay federal income tax on our taxable income at the corporate tax rate, which is currently a maximum of 21 percent, and likely would pay state and local income tax at varying rates.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss of partnership status or current corporate-tax obligation is demonstrated; the filing states that MPLX presently expects partnership treatment. This is a forward-looking structural risk. Its potential effect could be large because roughly half of operating value is terminal, but applying 21% directly to current owner earnings would not be supportable without taxable-income and state-tax calculations.
audit_findings.action: Document qualifying partnership status as an explicit terminal assumption and run a separate tax-conversion stress case using filed or tax-supported taxable income, the 21% federal rate, applicable state and local rates, and resulting changes to owner earnings and terminal value.
